summary:
Our project focuses on identifying potential locations on Earth with soil characteristics similar to those found on Mars. Through soil analysis and comparison, we explored terrestrial environments that could serve as analog sites for studying Martian soil conditions. 

Our goal is to identify locations that can help researchers better understand Martian soil, support future research, and provide valuable environments for testing and preparing technologies and strategies for future Mars exploration.
details:
How Does It Work?

How Does It Work?

The project uses NASA Earth observation datasets to analyze the surface and soil characteristics of Earth’s terrain, with the goal of finding areas that resemble Martian surface conditions. We incorporated several datasets, including:

  • EMIT L2B Mineral Identification: To investigate the mineral composition of the surface.
  • ASTER AG100: To analyze surface thermal emissivity.
  • SRTMGL1 / NASADEM: To obtain elevation data.
  • NASADEM Slope: To evaluate terrain slope and topography.
  • SMAP SPL3SMP: To analyze surface soil moisture.

Our method has three parts: characterizing Mars, characterizing Earth, and comparing the two.

  1. Mars reference

Mineralogy: We analyze the mineralogy of Mars using a spectrometer and thermal infrared data. For each mineral, the signal must be stronger than the noise and form patches. Each mineral is then classified as dominant, trace, or absent.

Terrain: We read a 3D elevation model and calculate slope and roughness

  1. Earth analysis

Mineralogy: We analyze Earth’s minerals using thermal infrared data. For each mineral, the signal must be stronger than the noise and form patches, and it is classified as dominant, trace, or absent. Thermal infrared sees the underlying bedrock, so vegetation, water, and areas where no minerals are detected are discarded. Each cell is scored on seven criteria: iron oxide, quartz, basalt, carbonates, two types of clay, and micas.

Terrain: We use an elevation map and soil moisture data to calculate slope and roughness.

  1. Comparison with Mars

Mineral comparison: We convert the scores into a percentage of similarity to Mars for each zone: the whole region, the lava field, the dunes, and the 10 best cells. A zone loses points for each criterion that does not match.

Terrain comparison: We compare the slope and roughness of each region.

By examining these different characteristics, we aim to identify terrestrial locations with conditions that resemble those observed on Mars.

 What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? 

  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, GitHub.
  • Programming languages: Python.
  • Infraestructure: GoDaddy (domain registration).
  • Frontend & UI: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

  • Claude: Coding, data analysis.
  • Gemini: Researching.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Identifying potential Martian analog sites on Earth can provide valuable opportunities for scientific research and experimentation. These locations could help researchers study geological conditions, test exploration technologies, and prepare for future missions to Mars.

Our project aims to support future robotic Mars exploration missions by identifying terrestrial locations with similar soil and surface characteristics. These locations could serve as testing environments where researchers can evaluate robotic systems, instruments, and exploration technologies under conditions that resemble those found on Mars, helping improve their preparation for future missions.

Factors Considered

Our analysis considers several characteristics that can influence the similarity between terrestrial and Martian environments, including mineral composition, elevation, terrain slope, and soil moisture.
